label: B25-EMIF-RESILIENCE
implementation_commits: 0a892c37 emif: bound Avalon abort and preserve response epoch
c660e13d verify: cover EMIF timeout and reset abort
7c47c221 emif: use synchronized CPU reset for epoch retention
4100cbcd verify: harden reset epochs and partial AXI writes
6864e0ae verify: split EMIF SVA reset epoch
objective: Complete every accepted AXI transaction exactly once with OKAY or DECERR across calibration abort, EMIF-only reset, Avalon stalls and missing read responses; hold AXI responses and prevent stale backend data from crossing epochs.

timeout_policy.vendor_latency_evidence: No Qsys/vendor EMIF worst-case waitrequest or readdatavalid latency upper bound exists in the checked-in platform manifest, Qsys snapshots, BFM, or existing tests; 32 cycles therefore cannot justify the production default.

rtl: Added parameterized AVALON_TIMEOUT_CYCLES with explicit timeout counter reset value 0 and terminal handling; production default is 4096 EMIF clocks (about 15.36 us at 266.666750 MHz), while the focused endpoint explicitly overrides it to 32.
Avalon waitrequest and missing readdatavalid timeouts emit one DECERR response packet; an accepted read enters EMIF_DRAIN and a late response is consumed without a second packet.
Retained read_issued_q/emif_poisoned_q across EMIF-only reset, synchronously sampled CPU reset as the explicit re-arm boundary, and synchronized poison to CPU-side request backpressure.
EMIF-only reset and synchronized calibration failure convert an in-flight CPU transaction to one DECERR instead of silently returning CPU_IDLE.
BVALID/RVALID and ID/data/RESP/LAST remain driven in response states independent of later calibration abort until BREADY/RREADY handshake.
Timeout abort is explicitly surfaced to the Avalon SVA checker so intentional command withdrawal is checked as a bounded protocol escape, not an assertion suppression.
bfm: Added cfg_drop_readdatavalid to model a permanently missing backend read response.
Added cfg_preserve_read_pending to retain an accepted response across an EMIF-only reset and verify late-response DRAIN; preserved counters in this mode.
verification: Updated the prior in-flight cal_fail test from no-response success to held DECERR with stable payload.
Added permanent waitrequest timeout, missing readdatavalid timeout plus late drain/re-arm, and EMIF-only reset DECERR/response-hold scenarios to both SV and Cocotb.

Late-response tests use different Avalon words/IDs with deterministic BFM initialization and check new data; AW-first and W-first partial writes pause across EMIF reset and complete exactly once after release.

The Avalon SVA checker now has separate CPU and EMIF reset semantics: CPU reset clears all state, while EMIF reset clears only stall/payload hold state and retains read_inflight epoch. A command asserted under waitrequest=0 is explicitly covered during EMIF-only reset.

review_closures: production timeout raised from 32 to 4096 EMIF cycles; focused endpoint remains 32
CPU reset re-arm uses cpu_rst_emif_meta_q/cpu_rst_emif_sync_q rather than raw sampling
different address/ID/data, partial AW/W and stalled-command reset tests eliminate prior false-green paths
SVA separates CPU epoch reset from EMIF command-hold reset
parent added ASYNC_REG markers, explicit SDC first-stage paths and design documentation

known_limits: No Quartus, fitter, TimeQuest, GamePC, JTAG, assembler, SOF, board or Linux run was performed; those regions are explicitly outside T-045.

The EMIF-only reset retention flag uses cpu_rst_emif_meta_q -> cpu_rst_emif_sync_q synchronous sampling in the EMIF clock domain; both stages have explicit power-up value 0, are not cleared by emif_rst_n, and the explicit CPU reset is the re-arm boundary. The CPU reset must remain asserted across the two emif_clk sampling edges.
The BFM models missing/late responses and reset retention; vendor EMIF-specific cancellation behavior still requires parent-level physical/integration validation.
risks: A backend that never returns a late response after an accepted read remains in EMIF_DRAIN by design; CPU request READY is blocked until an explicit CPU reset.
A calibration abort after an Avalon write acceptance cannot undo the external side effect; it reports DECERR exactly once and relies on higher-level retry/idempotence policy.
